Analyst report · Q3 2026 · Confidence medium

Bragg Gaming Group

A shrinking-but-cleaner quarter: revenue fell 23% to EUR 20.6m (~$23.4m) as the Dutch platform migrations removed EUR 6.2m (~$7.1m) on their own, while the mix shift away from aggregated third-party content lifted gross margin 155bps to 56%. Adj. EBITDA still dropped 33% to EUR 3.0m (~$3.4m) because EUR 1.6m (~$1.8m) of cost savings covered only half of the EUR 3.1m (~$3.5m) gross-profit loss, and cash is down to EUR 2.5m (~$2.8m) with capitalised development running ahead of operating cash flow. With the CEO replaced a week before the print and no guidance for FY26 or FY27, the case now rests on the interim CEO's cash discipline rather than growth.

PointsBet Holdings

A pre-announced miss delivered as pre-announced: H1 FY27 (Apr–Sep 2026) revenue fell 16% to A$112.7m (~US$79.2m) and normalised EBITDA swung from +A$2.9m (~US$2.0m) to -A$6.9m (~-US$4.9m), entirely driven by Australia, where self-imposed VIP compliance cuts took ~A$17m (~US$12m) out of net win and an 8.7% AFL/NRL-season hold in Aug–Sep cost roughly another A$6m (~US$4m). The more important disclosure is below the EBITDA line: corporate cash of A$5.3m (~US$3.7m), A$21m (~US$15m) of a A$23m parent facility drawn, net liabilities of A$34.8m (~US$24.5m) and going-concern language leaning on a MIXI letter of support — the equity story is now a funding story.

Analyst report · H1 FY27 · Confidence high

Konami Group

A clean beat on every line and the first mid-year guidance upgrade in 15 years: derived Q2 operating profit of ¥66.0bn (~$418m) was ~32% above the ~¥50bn market expectation and FY3/27 OP guidance moved from ¥143bn to ¥193bn (~$1.22bn), with 100% of the raise coming from Digital Entertainment (eFootball's World Cup window plus Yu-Gi-Oh! card demand). The debate now is durability, not delivery: management's own H2 implies DE business profit falling 25% from H1, Gaming & Systems guidance was left stale, and the equity's ~26x forward multiple rests on one live-service franchise holding a tournament-year cohort into a quadrennial comp.

Analyst report · 9M 2026 · Confidence medium

Philippine Amusement and Gaming Corporation

A 9M-26 print that is bad in level but no longer deteriorating: derived Q3 revenue of PHP 21.09bn (~$329m) was -15.8% YoY against -31.5% in Q2, with electronic-gaming revenue flat at ~PHP 9bn (~$141m) a quarter since the August-2025 e-wallet delinking reset the base. Net income of PHP 2.17bn (~$34m, -84.9%) reflects a structurally higher 5% PSC levy layered on a cost base that grew 3% while revenue fell 23% — the operating deleverage, not the court, is the bigger problem, and the FY26 H2 net-operating-income target now looks unattainable.

Analyst report · Q3 2026 · Confidence medium

BETBY

A volume-led quarter from an unlisted B2B supplier that discloses growth rates, not money: sportsbook GGR +33.4% YoY on actives +82.7% and bets +31.9% means GGR per active fell ~27% (our arithmetic) — breadth from new operator go-lives and World Cup/Esports World Cup casuals, not deeper monetisation. Growth has decelerated from +61% in Q1 and +42.7% in H1 but re-accelerated versus an implied ~+24% Q2 (est.), while lapping a soft-hold September 2025 comp. With no revenue, EBITDA, handle, hold, partner-count or concentration disclosure, this is a momentum signal, not an underwritable result.

Airtel Africa plc

A clean, high-quality half: revenue +28.2% reported / +20.8% constant currency to $3,823m, underlying EBITDA +32.8% to $1,921m with a record 50.4% Q2 margin despite a c.2–2.5pp fuel headwind, pre-exceptional EPS +41% to 11.7c and leverage down to 1.6x (0.5x lease-adjusted). The market nonetheless sold the shares c.5.5% to a new 52-week low: capex doubled to $657m, Nigeria decelerated (cc growth 24.4% in Q2 vs 29.8% in Q1, voice revenue down 6% QoQ), $55m of exceptionals hit PAT, and the NGN/ZMW translation tailwind that flattered reported growth expires in Q3. Guidance is unchanged (FY27 capex ~$1.1bn, margins "above 50%", dividend mid-to-high single-digit growth).

Monarch Casino & Resort

A record but decelerating quarter: net revenue +2.4% to $146.3m and adj. Analyst report · Q1 FY27 · Confidence medium

The Star Entertainment Group

The Star's Q1 FY27 (Sep-26 quarter) is the first positive EBITDA print in more than two years — A$12m (~$8m) vs –A$13m pcp — driven entirely by the two owned properties (Sydney + Gold Coast EBITDA A$35m / ~$24.5m, +164% YoY) and a 29% cut in unallocated corporate costs, partly offset by the Brisbane operator-fee reset (–67%). The operating turnaround is real but small: a ~A$48m annualised group EBITDA run-rate sits below our ~A$70m estimate of annual cash interest (currently paid from a restricted reserve), statutory operating cash flow was still –A$15.5m, cash fell A$28m to A$239m, and the day after the AGM the Federal Court imposed a A$260m (~$182m) AUSTRAC penalty that triggers a WhiteHawk review event. The equity remains a levered option on licence restoration and Bally's continued support, not a cash-flow story yet.

Market report · Q3 2026 · Confidence medium

United States

Q3 2026 is the quarter the regulated US online market stopped being a growth story and became a share-and-margin story: iGaming growth slowed to a record-low 12% YoY (Citizens; ~13-14% on summed state monthlies) with no new states since Rhode Island, and sportsbook handle was flat-to-down outside the June–July World Cup window while CFTC-regulated prediction markets printed >$82bn of September volume paying zero state gaming tax. For an entrant the addressable regulated pool is large (~$6.5–6.8bn/month commercial GGR, ~$1.0bn/month iGaming) but closed-access, high-tax, top-two dominated and now contested by an untaxed federal channel.

Market report · 9M 2026 · Confidence medium

Macau

Macau's 9M-2026 casino GGR of MOP187.12bn (~$23.19bn, +3.2% YoY) flatters a market that has rolled over: four straight monthly year-on-year declines through September (five through October), a Q3 of MOP60.22bn (~$7.46bn, -3.8%) driven by a 7.9% fall in mass/premium-mass baccarat, and GGR per visitor down ~5% even as arrivals rose 8.5%. The regime is stable but closed — six concessions locked to 31 Dec 2032, a 40% effective levy on GGR, zero licensed online — so for B2Tech the only realistic exposure is B2B supply into the one product line still growing, slots (+~19% YoY).

Market report · 2026 · Confidence medium

South Africa

South Africa is now a R84.5bn (~$5.1bn) GGR market whose growth is entirely online bookmaking: betting is 70% of GGR, ~86% of it online, and the land-based estate is shrinking. The rules are moving against the online channel — a proposed 20% national tax on online GGR (decision Feb 2027), new advertising norms, and an NGB site-blocking programme — while interactive casino remains illegal and licensing stays provincial. For B2Tech the prize is real but the licence-to-tax arbitrage that built the market is closing.

Market report · FIRST THREE MONTHS OF REGULATED MARKET · Confidence medium

Alberta

Alberta's open-licence online market generated C$122.1m (~$87.2m) of non-adjusted GGR on C$2,885m (~$2.06bn) of wagers in its first 80 days (13 Jul–30 Sep 2026), exiting September at C$56.6m (~$40.4m), +30.7% MoM, with only 24 operators live against 51 registered brands. It is a casino-led (78% of NAGGR), thin-hold (4.2%) land-grab with Ontario-parity economics (20% GGR share + 3% earmarks), but the regulator has not yet disclosed operator shares, the adjusted-GGR levy base or any channelization measurement — the headline is strong, the invoice is still open.

Market report · SEPTEMBER 2026 · Confidence medium

Tennessee

Tennessee's mobile-only sportsbook market took $591.9m of gross wagers in September 2026 (+4.7% YoY; taxable gross handle $588.6m, +4.9%) — the best month of 2026 but still short of the $598.6m booked in November 2024 — and yielded $10.88m of privilege tax under the only handle-based regime in the US (1.85% of gross handle). Growth has decelerated hard from the World Cup-inflated summer (+30–38% YoY in June/July) to mid-single digits, the licensed field has thinned to nine operators, and the regulatory story is now enforcement-led (a Sixth Circuit ruling that Tennessee's Sports Gaming Act reaches Kalshi's sports contracts, and a run of offshore cease-and-desists) rather than tax or licensing change. For an entrant, Tennessee is cheap to enter but structurally rewards scale and high-hold product; it penalises promo-heavy or low-margin models because free bets are taxed at face value.

Market report · Q3 2026 · Confidence medium

Alberta

Alberta's first 80 days as Canada's second open iGaming market produced C$2,885m (~$2,061m) of wagers and C$122.1m (~$87.2m) of non-adjusted GGR, with September alone at C$56.6m (~$40.4m) — a run-rate (~C$680m annualised) already ~1.7x the GGR implied by the government's own C$76m year-one revenue forecast. It is a casino-led market (78% of NAGGR) run on an Ontario-style conduct-and-manage model with a ~22% effective public take, cheap licences and the strictest day-one advertising rules in Canada; the swing factors from here are the Premier's threatened advertising clampdown, enforcement against the ~70% offshore base, and how 50 approved sites split a ~5m-person province.
